comparisons.objective: Extract and recover a trapped spacer with a pusher versus depinning one connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-tool pushing and pick-place versus dual-blade tang depression and coordinated wire pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Spacer nested and pusher parked versus selected terminal removed with housing, wire crimp, and neighbors preserved.
comparisons.reason: Generic tool-assisted extraction is shared, but the contact mechanics and required end state differ materially.

comparisons.objective: Select a wrench, release a captive nut, and open an arm versus depinning a terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool-size selection and rotary torque versus recessed blade insertion, tang depression, and axial pull.
comparisons.success_condition: Nut released without rounding, arm open, tools returned, 20-second hold versus selective terminal removal and 3-second release hold.
comparisons.reason: Fastener selection and rotary release do not test connector-terminal latch disengagement.

comparisons.objective: Remove a battery service plug and busbars in a safe order versus extracting one crimp terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plug removal and collision-safe busbar handling versus fine dual-blade insertion and simultaneous tool-wire withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Service plug removed before busbars, then bars safely trayed versus one terminal out with housing and neighbors intact.
comparisons.reason: Both involve electrical-component removal, but their mechanisms, sequencing, and final states are meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Release a spring clamp and recover its screwdriver versus depinning a connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clamp actuation and tool recovery versus recessed tang depression with sustained tool engagement and wire pulling.
comparisons.success_condition: Screwdriver held by the left gripper without drop or base motion versus terminal removed without wrong-terminal release or damage.
comparisons.reason: Shared release-and-pull primitives alone do not establish overlap; the tested contact strategy differs.

comparisons.objective: Route, buckle, and tighten a child-seat harness versus depinning a rigid connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Deformable webbing routing, buckle latching, and tensioning versus rigid-tool insertion and latch release.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct untwisted routing, latched buckle and clip, fit and hold versus selective terminal extraction with neighboring contacts retained.
comparisons.reason: The material mechanics, manipulation sequence, and functional outcome are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Route a connected cable between posts and secure its final clip versus remove a terminal from a connector.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual slack management and clip insertion versus dual-blade tang depression and coordinated extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Preserve the existing fixing, follow the route, seat the final clip, release and hold versus remove only the designated terminal without damage.
comparisons.reason: This record tests cable routing and retention, not terminal depinning.

comparisons.objective: Sort cubes while yielding shared space to a person's hand versus depinning a terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed collision avoidance and resumed pick-place versus close-tolerance blade insertion and force-controlled release.
comparisons.success_condition: No safety-envelope violation and all cubes sorted versus selective terminal removal with component integrity.
comparisons.reason: Human-aware temporal safety and connector servicing test different abilities.

comparisons.objective: Even wire tips and twist on a splice connector versus extract a crimp terminal from a housing.

comparisons.success_condition: Tips even, splice snug, and conductors retained versus one terminal removed while its crimp and housing remain intact.
comparisons.reason: Both manipulate wires, but splice formation is not latch-mediated depinning.

comparisons.objective: Drive a piston through a ring compressor into its bore versus extract a connector terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain compression and coaxial insertion versus recessed blade alignment, tang depression, and withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: All rings enter without escape or snag and the tool is released versus only the designated terminal exits without damage.
comparisons.reason: Compression-maintained insertion and latch-mediated removal are meaningfully different tested abilities.

comparisons.objective: Capture twelve-cell spring preload with a plate and cross-key versus depin one terminal.

comparisons.success_condition: All contacts compressed in range and key retained after release versus one terminal extracted while neighbors remain retained.

comparisons.objective: Seat an ear thermometer, trigger and hold a reading, then lay it down versus depin a terminal.

comparisons.objective: Lower a bent tube so four legs enter fixture slots together versus remove a terminal.

comparisons.success_condition: All legs rest on slot floors after release without a damaging drop versus selected terminal removed with housing and neighbors intact.

comparisons.objective: Release a camera from a cam-clamped mount and transfer it versus depin a connector terminal.

comparisons.success_condition: Camera and plate remain joined and rest safely on the receiving pad versus terminal exits while housing and adjacent terminals remain sound.
comparisons.reason: Both release retained parts, but the latch geometry, contact sequence, and final objective differ.

comparisons.objective: Immerse a wafer for a timed development interval and return it to heater pins versus depin a terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Plier grasping, vertical immersion, timer operation, and precision replacement versus blade insertion and latch release.
comparisons.success_condition: Continuous 28–32-second immersion with correct timer order and stable three-pin return versus selective damage-free extraction.

comparisons.objective: Join chain ends and install a retaining plate versus remove one connector terminal.

comparisons.objective: Close double doors in order and engage their bolt and latch versus depin a terminal.

comparisons.success_condition: Both leaves closed in the required order, bolt and latch engaged, then released and still versus selective terminal extraction.
